notes: Intro: Nebula Rankline builds an AI-first KB and search layer for mid-market SaaS vendors. Primary product is an embeddable support search widget + analytics dashboard.

Summary: evaluation focused on embeddings + reranking pipeline (dense retrieval -> 50-200 candidate docs -> transformer reranker). High sustained QPS during GTM peaks (10k rps read across multi-tenant customers).

Quote from CTO: "We can tolerate occasional 200ms tails on long reranks, but median rerank should be <120ms at 99th-percentile target during non-peak; cost per query needs to stay under $0.01 to be unit-economically viable."
Deployment preference: prefer Redwood hosted API initially for time-to-value; willing to revisit Dedicated if latency/SLA or data residency becomes an issue.
Security: strict audit logging, SSO/SAML integration required; encryption + KMS enforced by legal for SOC2 compliance.

POC ask: index ~2M support docs (PDFs, HTML pages, policy docs). Expect average doc length 800 tokens, median retrieval set 100 candidates. Need to validate hybrid reranking throughput using Redwood Optimize suggestions (batching, KV cache, quant profiles).
Cost sensitivity: finance wants modeled cost at 10k QPS sustained (burst to 25k) — target annualized token spend under $150k for early customers once amortized across tenanting model.

Integration notes: existing infra uses GCP us-central; current vector store is self-hosted Pinecone (trial). Engineering wants a drop-in test with minimal schema changes; prefers REST + SDK for server-side calls.
Sales angle: upsell path is Dedicated + extended retention for enterprise customers; early win if hosted meets 99th p99 latency SLA and shows predictable unit-costs.
Objections: concern about fallback routing — they'd want automatic cheaper model fallback for non-critical queries, plus deterministic billing visibility per route.
Action items recorded: Jordan to share perf-key, Lina to run baseline tests, engineering to send credentials for synthetic load (JMeter scripts).

requirements_summary: Indexing scale: target 1.5-2.5M docs initially; plan to grow to ~10M over 12 months
Embedding store: dense vectors (~1536 dim) for retriever; expect 100M+ vectors in 12 months — want compaction/quantization options
Reranking: transformer reranker on top of retrieval; typical candidate set 50-200; strict latency targets: median <80ms, p99 <250ms for reranker
Throughput: high sustained QPS — baseline 5k-10k qps, peak bursts to 25k qps; multitenant isolation desired
Cost targets: blended cost-per-query goal <$0.01 (prefer <$0.005) including retrieval+rerank; finance requires modeled scenarios
Routing/fallback: automatic fallback to cheaper model variant for non-critical queries; regional routing to reduce egress/latency
Observability: token-level cost breakdown, per-route latency histograms, tracing for rerank steps
Compliance: SOC2, SSO/SAML, audit logs retention for 12 months, KMS-managed keys
decision_criteria: Meets latency SLO at target QPS (p99 rerank <250ms)
Predictable cost model with line-item for rerank vs retrieval
Security controls: SSO + audit logging + KMS proof
Operational ease: minimal integration lift and SDK parity
Path to Dedicated with SLA language if hosted can't meet peak latency
